data.name: Jayanand
data.gender_notes: Jayanand is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Jaya: victory, anand: to the lord. This name is derived from the Sanskrit language and carries a deep spiritual meaning, representing the devotion and surrender to the divine. The name Jayanand carries the meaning “Victory to the lord” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jayanand usually hope their child will grow to embody victory to the lord and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: Jayanand was a renowned Sanskrit scholar and poet from the 13th century in South India. He is best known for his work 'Jayamangalasutra', a Sanskrit encyclopedia of all aspects of life including literature, art, music, and sciences.

Jayanand was also a Jain scholar who composed various commentaries on Jain texts, including the 'Bhagavati-sutra' and 'Tattvartha-sutra'. He played a significant role in the preservation and propagation of Jainism during the medieval period in India.
